record_type_quote: Based on our previous research, the aim of this study was to test whether 5HTTLPR genotype was associated with outcome following CBT in a large replication sample of 829 children with anxiety disorders.

targets.authors: Eley TC, Hudson JL, Creswell C, Tropeano M, Lester KJ, Cooper P, et al.
targets.title: Therapygenetics: the 5HTTLPR and response to psychological therapy.
targets.evidence_quote: Finally, logistic and linear mixed models were run using participants from both Cohort 1 15 and Cohort 2 combined. A total of 584 samples were genotyped in Cohort 1, from children (aged 6-13) who received CBT for an anxiety disorder. In this sample, 496 had sufficient outcome data to be included in at least one analysis. The sample size of 359 reported in Eley et al 8 refers to the White European participants included in the main analysis of response to therapy at follow-up.
targets.outcome_quote: The association between 5HTTLPR genotype and CBT outcome did not replicate. Short-allele homozygotes showed more positive treatment outcomes, but with small, non-significant effects.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall non-replication verdict for the independent cohort determines the outcome; pooled mega-analysis does not reverse the independent replication verdict.
